recipe.notes: cognee 1.6.2 defaults (infrastructure/llm/config.py llm_model, embeddings/config.py DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL; dims derived by litellm). LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL, LLM_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL and LLM_QUERY_MODEL stay unset, so every stage uses the base model. GRAPH_EXTRACTOR=llm pins LLM extraction; without it a missing key would select the local GLiNER demo extractor and fastembed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5.

common.notes: LLM_MODEL, EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS set by shim.py; cognee forwards dimensions to the embeddings API (LiteLLMEmbeddingEngine).

time_notes: Each turn-pair item carries 'Time anchor: <event_time>' in its text, as cognee's BEAM preprocessing does. temporal_cognify stays off, as in cognee's BEAM ingestion. cognee.search takes no query date, so query_time is ignored and applied_settings says so. A null event_time (allowed by the protocol) is written as 'Time anchor: unknown'; cognee never substitutes the ingest time, because dates live only in the text.

provenance.mechanism: Chunk items carry payload.document_id, which is the cognee Data id. The shim pins each session's Data id (uuid5 of namespace and source id) through DataItem.data_id and labels it with the source id, so a chunk maps to exactly one session (exact). Entity and fact items come from the merged graph and carry no source; they are returned with provenance unavailable. The map is rebuilt from cognee.datasets.list_data labels (public API) after a restart.

delete_notes: cognee.forget(data_id, dataset) removes the Data row and its chunks and chunk vectors; after it no chunk from the deleted session returns. In the keyless check (canned extraction), graph entities shared with a surviving session stayed and their edge text still quoted the deleted session; in the metered smoke (real extraction) no entity or fact mentioned the deleted fact. lifecycle-lite should score entity and fact items as well as chunks.
readiness: synchronous: /ingest runs cognee.add then cognee.cognify(run_in_background=False) for that session, as cognee's BEAM local_ingest does, so /finish has nothing to wait for. A failed pipeline raises (raise_on_error=True) and becomes a product_error.
namespace: dataset (one cognee dataset per namespace, named by the opaque ns id; ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL is on by default, so each dataset gets its own graph and vector store)

vendor-default.maps_to: cognee.search(query_type=HYBRID_COMPLETION, only_context=True, verbose=True, datasets=[ns]). search top_k 15 caps each hybrid lane at min(15, DEFAULT_HYBRID_LANE_TOP_K=10): 10 chunks, 10 entities with up to 10 edges each, 10 facts. HYBRID_COMPLETION is recall()'s fallback type (ROUTER_FALLBACK_TYPE) and the retriever cognee selected for its reported BEAM configuration. The type is pinned (auto_route off) so the item shape is deterministic.

fixed-evidence.maps_to: cognee.search(query_type=HYBRID_COMPLETION, only_context=True, verbose=True, datasets=[ns]). 20 chunks, 20 entities (cognee's reported BEAM 100K configuration hybrid_completion_20_20_qa_v1), 10 facts; the harness packs the returned items to the 8,000-token budget. Why: the largest documented hybrid setting; the harness truncates to the shared budget

retrieval_notes.item_order: chunks (cognee rank), then entities, then facts, the order cognee renders them into its own context string (raw.context)

agent_surface.version: cognee-mcp 0.5.6 (not built in this lane; Phase 8)

deviations_from_vendor_code: Session documents are added as JSON text through DataItem (with a pinned data_id and the source id as label) instead of a JSON file on disk; JsonListChunker reads the same JSON list either way.
Turns are paired in arrival order (1-2, 3-4, ...) and labelled by speaker; cognee's BEAM code pairs user and assistant turns. LoCoMo has two named speakers and no assistant.
The item header keeps Session/Turn/Time anchor but the session number is the ingestion order inside the namespace, not a dataset session id.

No BEAM turn compression, no session distillation and no global context index: they are BEAM-specific additions in local_ingest.py, not part of add + cognify, and the reported 100K retrieval did not query the global index.

cognee.search with verbose=True is used instead of cognee.recall: for only_context completion types recall returns one rendered prompt string, while search(verbose=True) returns the same retrieval as separate ranked chunks, entities and facts with chunk document ids.
No per-question-type answer prompts: the harness's fixed reader answers.

AMB's cognee provider (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark@f618ed7) ingests all documents then cognifies once and retrieves CHUNKS top 50 with fastembed; this shim follows cognee's own BEAM code instead because it exercises the graph.
